question: Which body activities does the autonomic nervous system control?

options.B: Sensory perception of sharp skin pain

explanation: The autonomic nervous system handles automatic body processes without conscious direction. [learn more](BMP121_U5_T4#BMP121_U5_T4_h1)

question: Why is maintaining homeostasis the main goal of the autonomic nervous system?

options.A: It prepares the skeletal muscles for heavy exercise
options.B: It stops all organ activity during times of deep sleep
options.C: It speeds up digestion whenever a person feels stressed
options.D: It keeps internal body conditions stable and balanced

explanation: The sympathetic and parasympathetic divisions balance each other to keep the body's internal environment stable. [learn more](BMP121_U5_T4#BMP121_U5_T4_h1)

question: Where do the early nerve fibers of the sympathetic nervous system start?

options.A: Thoracolumbar region of the spinal cord
options.B: Skeletal muscle tissue fibers in the limbs
options.C: Craniosacral region of the central nervous system
options.D: Cerebral cortex of the frontal brain lobe

explanation: Sympathetic preganglionic cell bodies are found specifically in the thoracic and upper lumbar spinal segments. [learn more](BMP121_U5_T4#BMP121_U5_T4_h2)

question: How do parasympathetic nerve pathways generally compare to sympathetic ones?

options.A: Parasympathetic pathways possess very short preganglionic nerve fibers
options.B: Parasympathetic pathways do not use any form of ganglionic synapses
options.C: Parasympathetic pathways originate entirely within the lumbar spinal cord
options.D: Parasympathetic pathways have long preganglionic and short postganglionic fibers

explanation: Parasympathetic preganglionic fibers travel a long distance to reach ganglia situated right next to or inside the target organ. [learn more](BMP121_U5_T4#BMP121_U5_T4_h2)

question: What happens in the body when the sympathetic nervous system is activated?

options.C: Constriction of the pupil of the eye
options.D: Increased blood flow to the gut

explanation: Sympathetic activation widens the airways to allow more oxygen entry during high-energy states. [learn more](BMP121_U5_T4#BMP121_U5_T4_h3)

question: A labouring woman is feeling very frightened and anxious. Which bodily response is expected from her sympathetic nervous system?

options.A: Faster heart rate and elevated blood pressure
options.B: Increased digestive activity and heavy salivation
options.C: Immediate constriction of her pupils in bright light
options.D: Enhanced blood flow shifting strictly to her intestines

explanation: Fear triggers the sympathetic fight-or-flight response, which speeds up the heart and raises blood pressure. [learn more](BMP121_U5_T4#BMP121_U5_T4_h3)

question: What is the main job of the parasympathetic nervous system?

options.B: Preparing the body for sudden physical combat
options.C: Triggering massive adrenaline release into blood
options.D: Spiking blood glucose levels for fast running

explanation: The parasympathetic division manages resting functions, energy storage, and digestion. [learn more](BMP121_U5_T4#BMP121_U5_T4_h4)

question: How do parasympathetic responses differ from sympathetic responses in the body?

options.A: Parasympathetic pathways always use short preganglionic fibers
options.B: Parasympathetic effects are localized rather than generalized body-wide reactions
options.C: Parasympathetic nerves directly stimulate skeletal muscle contraction
options.D: Parasympathetic activation stops all metabolic activity entirely

explanation: Parasympathetic fibers stimulate individual organs separately, unlike the widespread mass activation of the sympathetic system. [learn more](BMP121_U5_T4#BMP121_U5_T4_h4)

question: Which chemical messenger is released by all autonomic preganglionic nerve fibers?
explanation: Acetylcholine is the chemical messenger used at all autonomic ganglia by preganglionic fibers of both systems. [learn more](BMP121_U5_T4#BMP121_U5_T4_h5)

question: Where are muscarinic receptors typically found in the autonomic nervous system?

options.A: At synapses inside the sympathetic and parasympathetic ganglia
options.B: On target organs of the parasympathetic nervous system
options.C: Inside the central nervous system preganglionic cell bodies
options.D: Directly on the cell membranes of skeletal muscle fibers

explanation: Muscarinic receptors respond to acetylcholine at parasympathetic effector tissues, whereas nicotinic receptors sit on ganglia. [learn more](BMP121_U5_T4#BMP121_U5_T4_h5)

question: What does 'dual innervation' mean for an organ?

options.A: It is controlled entirely by conscious somatic motor pathways
options.B: It possesses two separate hearts beating at different rates
options.C: It receives nerve fibers from both sympathetic and parasympathetic divisions
options.D: It uses both acetylcholine and adrenaline at the exact same receptor

explanation: Dual innervation means an organ gets inputs from both parts of the autonomic nervous system to finely tune its function. [learn more](BMP121_U5_T4#BMP121_U5_T4_h6)

question: Which of the following body parts is an exception because it usually receives ONLY sympathetic nerve supply?

options.B: The smooth muscle of the stomach
options.C: The muscular wall of the heart
options.D: The circular iris muscle of the eye

explanation: Most blood vessels and sweat glands rely solely on sympathetic tone for regulation rather than dual input. [learn more](BMP121_U5_T4#BMP121_U5_T4_h6)

question: How can high anxiety and fear negatively affect a woman's progress in labour?

options.A: Sympathetic overactivation can reduce uterine blood flow and slow contractions
options.B: Excessive acetylcholine release causes immediate exhaustion of skeletal muscles
options.C: Parasympathetic dominance instantly stops all cervical dilation permanently
options.D: Vagal nerve stimulation completely prevents any sensation of uterine pain

explanation: Fear triggers sympathetic fight-or-flight activity, releasing hormones that divert blood from the uterus and can impede labour progress. [learn more](BMP121_U5_T4#BMP121_U5_T4_h7)

question: A midwife keeps the labour room quiet, dims the lights, and speaks softly to a stressed mother. What is the main physiological goal of this care?

options.A: To force a rapid switch to sympathetic fight-or-flight status
options.B: To block all sensory nerve pathways coming from the pelvis
options.C: To reduce sympathetic activity and encourage relaxation
options.D: To stimulate nicotinic receptors inside the autonomic ganglia

explanation: A calm, soothing environment reduces maternal stress and dampens excess sympathetic tone, aiding normal labour physiology. [learn more](BMP121_U5_T4#BMP121_U5_T4_h7)
